cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest living among the exiles, far from home (Ezekiel 1:1-3). In the sixth year, he's sitting in his house with the elders of Judah sitting before him. And right there, in the middle of company, the hand of the Lord GOD falls on him.
Ezekiel looks and sees a figure like that of a man. From His waist down, His appearance is like fire, and from His waist up, He's as bright as the gleam of amber.
He stretches out what looks like a hand and takes Ezekiel by the hair of his head. The HAIR, friend, and with a mustache this size, I felt that one all the way down to my gold base.

cards.question: Then the Spirit lifts Ezekiel up between earth and heaven and carries him in visions of God to ___.
Ezekiel ends up at the entrance of the north gate of the inner court. What's there?
There in Jerusalem, Ezekiel sees something just like the vision he saw back in the plain. What is it?

answers.text: The glory of the God of Israel

cards.text: God tells Ezekiel, "now lift up your eyes to the north." Ezekiel does, and there in the entrance north of the Altar Gate is that idol of jealousy.

cards.question: God says the house of Israel is committing these great abominations to drive Him far from His sanctuary.
God has just shown Ezekiel the idol of jealousy at the north gate. What does God tell Ezekiel he will still see?

answers.text: The people turning back to Him

cards.text: Next, God brings Ezekiel to the entrance to the court, and Ezekiel spots a hole in the wall. It's just a hole, friend, and I'm ALREADY nervous.

cards.question: At the hole in the wall, God tells Ezekiel to leave the wall alone and just peek through the hole.

cards.text: So Ezekiel digs through the wall and finds a doorway.

God tells him to go in and see the wicked abominations they're committing there. Ezekiel looks, and engraved all around the wall is every kind of crawling creature and detestable beast, along with all the idols of the house of Israel.

cards.question: Ezekiel digs through a wall into a room engraved with crawling creatures, detestable beasts and idols. Who's standing in front of those engravings?

cards.text: Jaazaniah son of Shaphan stands among them. Each man has a censer in his hand, and a fragrant cloud of incense is rising.
God asks Ezekiel if he sees what the elders of Israel are doing in the darkness, each at the shrine of his own idol.

cards.question: The elders in that dark room are saying the LORD sees everything they do.
The elders burning incense in that dark room also say the LORD has ___ the land.

cards.text: Again, God tells Ezekiel he'll see them committing even greater abominations. Then He brings Ezekiel to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD.

cards.question: At the north gate of the house of the LORD, Ezekiel sees ___ sitting there, weeping for Tammuz, a false god.

cards.text: God asks him, "do you see this?" and says he'll see even greater abominations than these. Then He brings Ezekiel into the inner court, to the entrance to the temple of the LORD, between the portico and the altar.

cards.question: About twenty-five men are standing between the portico and the altar. They're facing the temple of the LORD.
With their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east, what are these twenty-five men bowing to in worship?

cards.text: God asks Ezekiel, "do you see this?" Then He asks if the abominations they're practicing here aren't enough for the house of Judah.

cards.question: God asks if the abominations in the temple aren't enough for the house of Judah. Where else does He say they're doing wrong?

answers.text: Down in the land of Egypt

cards.text: They fill the land with violence and keep provoking Him to anger. And then one more: "Look, they are even putting the branch to their nose!"

cards.question: After everything God has shown Ezekiel, how does God say He will respond?
God says that although they shout loudly in His ears, He will not listen to them.

cards.text: That's a lot to take in, friend. But hold on, because this story isn't over yet.
